conference.name: ACM AI Leadership Summit 2026
conference.dataNote: Unofficial schedule snapshot reconstructed from ACM's public summit announcements (April–August 2026). Session times and rooms are illustrative, not authoritative; the official program lives at aisummit.acm.org.

sessions.title: Registration & Badge Pickup
Doctoral Consortium: Nurturing Future Leaders of AI (Morning)
sessions.description: A full day of mentorship, research guidance, and peer exchange for doctoral students, led by the researchers and policymakers headlining the summit.

sessions.title: Doctoral Consortium: Nurturing Future Leaders of AI (Afternoon)
sessions.description: One-on-one mentoring circles and a career panel with senior researchers from academia and industry.

sessions.title: Future Leaders Orientation
sessions.description: Welcome and orientation for the Future Leaders cohort: how to get the most out of the summit's four days.

sessions.title: Welcome Reception
Registration & Coffee
Opening Remarks: Why an AI Leadership Summit, Why Now
Keynote: Beyond Autoregression — Paths Toward Machines That Understand the World
speakers: Yann LeCun (ACM A.M. Turing Award Laureate)
sessions.description: A Turing laureate's view of the next generation of AI models, architectures, and paradigms reshaping the boundaries of machine intelligence.

sessions.title: Coffee Break
Rethinking the Future: New Architectures and Paradigms
sessions.description: An exploration of the next generation of AI models, architectures, and paradigms reshaping the boundaries of intelligence and scientific research.

sessions.title: AI as a Catalyst for Scientific Breakthroughs
sessions.description: How AI is reshaping the conduct of research across disciplines, from hypothesis generation to lab automation.

sessions.title: AI for Software Development: The Agentic Turn
sessions.description: Where AI-assisted engineering actually stands: coding agents, verification, and what changes for professional developers.

sessions.title: Teaching Computing When Machines Can Code
sessions.description: Curricula, assessment, and academic integrity in the age of capable AI assistants.

sessions.title: Lunch
Fireside Chat: AI and the Transformation of Work
speakers: Jaime Teevan (Chief Scientist & Technical Fellow, Microsoft)
sessions.description: How organizations are rebuilding workflows, tools, and teams around AI, and what the research says about productivity and skill.

sessions.title: AI for Infrastructure & Systems: Compute, Energy, and Scale
sessions.description: The systems underneath the models: datacenter economics, energy constraints, and efficient inference.

sessions.title: AI & Society: Measuring Real-World Impact
sessions.description: Parallel track addressing societal impact: labor, information ecosystems, and equitable access.

sessions.title: AI for Science: Foundation Models for Discovery
sessions.description: Domain foundation models in biology, materials, and climate science, and how to evaluate them.

sessions.title: Coffee Break
Panel: Governing AI Across Borders
speakers: Amandeep Singh Gill (UN Secretary-General's Envoy on Technology)
sessions.description: Global governance, ethics, and policy coordination for AI: what international institutions can and cannot do.

sessions.title: Poster Session & Reception
sessions.description: Posters from the Papers Track and the Doctoral Consortium, with light refreshments.

sessions.title: Keynote: Reinforcement Learning, Then and Now
speakers: Andrew Barto (ACM A.M. Turing Award Laureate)
sessions.description: A Turing laureate reflects on the ideas behind reinforcement learning and what they suggest about the road ahead.

sessions.title: Coffee Break
Papers Track I: Advances in AI Systems
sessions.description: Peer-reviewed papers showcasing cutting-edge advances and forward-looking ideas in AI from academia and industry.

sessions.title: Papers Track II: AI Applications and Impact
sessions.description: Peer-reviewed papers on applied AI: deployment experience, measurement, and lessons from practice.

sessions.title: Responsible AI in Practice: From Principles to Process
sessions.description: Turning governance frameworks into engineering practice: evaluations, red-teaming, and incident response.

sessions.title: AI & Education: Tutors, Feedback, and Equity
sessions.description: Evidence on AI tutoring and automated feedback, and who benefits when they are deployed at scale.

sessions.title: Lunch & Birds-of-a-Feather Tables
Keynote: AI and the Future of Storytelling
speakers: Markus Gross (Chief Scientist, Walt Disney Studios)
sessions.description: How AI is changing production, animation, and interactive media at one of the world's largest studios.

sessions.title: AI for Software Development: Trust, Testing, and Provenance
sessions.description: Keeping engineering rigor when much of the code is machine-written: reviews, tests, and supply-chain provenance.

sessions.title: AI for Infrastructure & Systems: Reliability at Scale
sessions.description: Operating AI in production: reliability engineering, observability, and graceful degradation.

sessions.title: AI & Society: Information Integrity and Public Trust
sessions.description: Synthetic media, provenance standards, and rebuilding trust in the information ecosystem.

sessions.title: Coffee Break
Panel: Workforce Transformation and the Computing Profession
sessions.description: What AI means for computing careers, professional identity, and the pipeline of new talent.

sessions.title: Summit Banquet
Keynote: What AI Still Cannot Do
sessions.description: A robotics pioneer on the gap between demos and deployment, and the hard problems that remain.

sessions.title: Coffee Break
Rethinking the Future: Agents, Autonomy, and Alignment
sessions.description: Agentic systems and their safety cases: capability frontiers, oversight, and open research problems.

sessions.title: AI for Science: Reproducibility and Open Ecosystems
sessions.description: Open models, open data, and keeping AI-accelerated science verifiable.

sessions.title: Policy Roundtable: National Strategies for AI Research
sessions.description: Funding agencies and policymakers on sustaining public-interest AI research.

sessions.title: Lunch
Town Hall: Shaping ACM's AI Agenda
sessions.description: An open community discussion: what the computing community should do next, and how ACM can help.

sessions.title: Closing Remarks
